# Working on `shop`

Written by `sofie gen` from the code; `sofie check` reports it stale when the code changes. Ask `sofie explain NAME` before reading files.

## Modules

- `order` (Core) in `modules/order/`; areas `customer`; aggregates `AuditEntry`, `Order`; events `OrderPlaced`, `OrderCancelled`; contract `order-contract`

## Areas

- `web`: at the root, defined by the framework
- `customer`: under `/account`, defined by `order-contract`

Route paths in `routes` and `explain` are full, with the area's prefix; generators such as `sofie new route` take a path relative to the area's prefix: `/orders/{order}` for `/account/orders/{order}` in an area under `/account`.

## Commands

- `sofie gen`: rewrites the generated files (wiring, contracts' `gen/`, `.env.example`, this file); run it after changing routes, modules, aggregates or screens.
- `sofie check`: every rule below; `app/build.rs` runs it, so a finding fails `cargo build`.
- `sofie fix`: applies the fixes that have exactly one form, then reports the rest.
- `sofie explain NAME`: a route, area, module, event, job, task, read model, aggregate, screen, screen component or flag.
- `sofie routes`: the route table.
- `sofie components`: every component a screen template may use, with its props, and the template syntax.
- `sofie tasks`: each `#[task]` with the `--name value` arguments it reads; the binary runs one with `<app> task MODULE.NAME [--name value]...`.
- `sofie dev`: runs the app, rebuilding and reloading on changes.
- `sofie feature add|remove NAME`: turns a `sofie` feature on or off in `app/Cargo.toml`, editing only that dependency's features.
- `sofie new module NAME`, `sofie scaffold tests`, `sofie scaffold screen KEY`: new code in its place, wired.
- `sofie new migration MODULE NAME`, `sofie new aggregate MODULE Name`, `sofie new event MODULE Name`, `sofie new listener MODULE Event handler`, `sofie new task MODULE handler`, `sofie new search MODULE Aggregate`, `sofie new plan MODULE name`, `sofie new mail MODULE name [--list LIST]`, `sofie new area MODULE NAME ACCESS`, `sofie new account-screen AREA SCREEN`, `sofie new impersonation PERMITTED_AREA MEMBER_AREA`, `sofie new tenancy ORGANIZATION_AREA MEMBER_AREA`, `sofie new route MODULE AREA METHOD PATH handler [--screen NAME] [--fields FIELDS] [--read-model Name] [--title TITLE] [--back HANDLER]`, `sofie new menu MODULE AREA handler LABEL`: stubs in their place, then `sofie gen` and `sofie check`.
- `sofie build [--image]`: the release binary, and with `--image` its container image.
- `sofie bench`: load tests of the routes, held to a baseline.
- `sofie fuzz [--seed N] [--requests N]`: sends every route generated valid and broken inputs, signed in and out, and reports each 500, dropped answer or crash with its input, span tree and log lines; a local database only.
- `sofie seed [--volume N]`: fills the local database through the app's own POST routes, first with each module's `seeds/<area>.<handler>.json` (a JSON array of inputs), then N generated inputs per route, as the member `sofie bench` signs in with.
- `sofie mcp`: these tools over the Model Context Protocol, each generator with `dry_run`, and the app's own tools below.
- `cargo test --offline`: the tests.

## Running the app through `sofie mcp`

- Before calling a route, `explain` it: it names the input's fields and their JSON shape.
- `request` runs the app itself on a free local port and rebuilds it when code changed, so there is no need to start `sofie dev`. Its `session` is a named cookie jar: sign up or in through the app's own routes, then act as that user. With `target`, the id a `Form` or `Action` targets, it asks for that fragment alone. The answer carries the request's span tree; jobs and listeners of the same trace come later through `traces` with its trace id.
- `dev` starts, stops or reports the app; `logs` follows its output with a cursor; `traces` lists recent span trees, requests apart from jobs and listeners.
- `task` runs one `#[task]` once against the app's database, as `<app> task` does; its `arguments` are a JSON object.
- `tests` lists each test file of the app and its modules with its test functions; with `name` it answers one test's source. Read the nearest one before writing a test, and follow its style.
- `test` answers each test that ran by name and outcome; with `filter`, also the tests in changed files the filter left out, so run those too.
- `lint` runs `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on the app's own packages (with `write` it formats them first); run it with `check` and `test` before calling work done.
- `changes` lists the files added, modified, renamed or deleted under the app root since git's last commit, and with `path` one file's diff: review it before calling work done.
- `db_status`: call it before and after adding or changing a migration; it shows per module which migrations are applied, pending, edited after being applied or missing as files. Never edit an applied migration: add a new one, or rebuild a local database with `sofie db fresh`.
- The app needs `DATABASE_URL` and `SOFIE_SIGNING_KEYS` from the environment or `.env`.

## Where code goes

Under `modules/<module>/`:

- `src/module.rs`: `MODULE`, the manifest (name, tier, settings) spreading the generated `src/wiring.rs`; `src/config.rs`: its configuration.
- `src/<aggregate>/mod.rs`: an aggregate, changed only through its methods; `factory.rs` beside it is its only constructor.
- `src/actions/`: one file per action (writes); `src/queries/`: one per query (reads) and their read models.
- `src/areas/<area>/routes.rs`: the module's endpoints in an area; `menu.rs` its menu entries; `screens/<name>.html` its templates.
- `src/tasks.rs` or `src/tasks/`: `#[task]` functions run once by hand, such as a data backfill.
- `src/gateways/`: outgoing requests; `src/extensions/`: implementations of other contracts' extension points; `src/domain/`: private code.
- `contract/`: the only crate other modules may use: traits, events (`events.rs`), areas (`area.rs`); `contract/src/gen/` is generated.
- `migrations/NNNN_name.sql`, `lang/<language>.toml`.

`app/src/wiring.rs` and each module's `src/wiring.rs` are generated; the app crate holds no module code.

## Rules `sofie check` holds the app to

- A module uses another module only through its contract crate; tiers depend downward (Experience, Core, Platform) and nothing depends on the app.
- A Platform module never listens to events of modules above it; events are declared in contracts.
- Only queries are routed under `get`; SQL is written only in queries; no two endpoints share a path in an area.
- Code asks for `Clock` instead of reading the system time, and reads the environment only through its module's config.
- Requests leave the app only through gateways and contracts.
- Every field constraint and enum of an aggregate has a CHECK or unique index in a migration.
- Screens bind only what their loader provides; flags are named `<module>.<flag>` and declared by their module with the day they were added.
- No dead code or unused dependency (unless `dead-code-allow.toml` gives a reason); an app setting `structure-ceilings = true` also keeps comments within 2.86% of code lines and no type a god type.
- Generated files are current: run `sofie gen`.

## How to add

- A module: `sofie new module NAME`, then set its tier in `src/module.rs`.
- A route: `sofie new route`, or one line in `src/areas/<area>/routes.rs` naming a handler in `actions/` or `queries/`, such as `routes.post("/orders", actions::place_order)`; then `sofie gen`.
- A screen: `sofie new route MODULE AREA get PATH handler --screen NAME` (a path naming an aggregate, such as `/orders/{order}`, gets a read model of its fields and a screen showing them; `--fields a,b` picks them), or `src/areas/<area>/screens/<name>.html` routed with `routes.screen("/path", "<name>", queries::loader)`; then `sofie gen`.
- An aggregate: `sofie new aggregate`, or `src/<aggregate>/mod.rs` with `#[derive(Aggregate)]`, re-exported from `lib.rs`, and a migration creating its table; then `sofie gen` and `sofie check`.
- An event and its listener: `sofie new event`, then `sofie new listener` in each module reacting to it.
- Tests: `sofie scaffold tests` writes them for what the modules declare. Scaffolded tests live in `app/tests/scaffolded/`, one file per run; extend them there; hand-written tests go in `app/tests/<topic>.rs`. Write each as `#[test_app] async fn name(app: TestApp)`, as the scaffolded ones are; `#[tokio::test]` only where `#[test_app]` cannot run it, with a line saying why.

## Loaders, read models and screens

- A loader is an `async fn` in `queries/` that takes `read: Read` (and route parameters) and answers a read model, or a `Vec`, `Option`, `Paginated` or `Listed` of one; `sofie gen` checks every screen binding against that type without compiling, so any other type is a finding. A loader taking `listing: Listing<Row>` answers `listing.page(&read).await`, which a `Table` pages, sorts and filters; a GET takes no `Input`, so it reads the query string as `query: sofie::http::Query<Search>`, `Search` a `#[derive(Input)]` struct checked as a body is (a listing takes `Listing<Row, Search>` and reads it with `listing.parameters()`).
- `#[derive(ReadModel)]` with `#[read(from = Order)]` selects those columns of an aggregate: `OrderRow::query().where_(…).latest().limit(50).all(&read)`, also `first`, `count`, `exists`; `all` without `limit` reads every match, and `stream` (the `sofie` feature `streams`, no ordering or limit) is only for more rows than fit in memory. `Status::VARIANTS` lists an `#[derive(Enum)]`'s `(name, value)` pairs, e.g. to show statuses with no records. Reads are already scoped to what the principal may see, so a loader never filters by owner itself. Everything a read model selects reaches JSON and tables, so a field reading a sensitive one is a compile error unless it is marked `#[sensitive]`.
- Without `#[read(from = …)]` a read model is computed: the loader fills its fields, so counts, sums and groupings are plain Rust over rows it read, e.g. `OrderSummary { by_status: Vec<StatusCount>, total: Money }` with `StatusCount` a computed read model too; bindings are checked through both. Never change the framework's crates; report what it lacks.
- Templates only access fields and format them; compute everything in the loader.
- With `sofie mcp` connected, write scaffolding through its generate tools (`dry_run` first), not by hand; fill in the bodies they leave.
- Through `sofie mcp`, `edit_screen` changes an existing screen template by key: it replaces an exact `find` text that occurs once with `replace`, then runs `sofie gen` and `sofie check` (`dry_run` first).
- A menu entry: `sofie new menu MODULE AREA handler LABEL` (MCP `new_menu_entry`) writes it, declares the file and enables the feature. It goes in `src/areas/<area>/menu.rs`, which holds only `pub fn menu(menu: &mut Menu<Area>) { menu.entry("Label", <module>_contract::routes::<area>::<handler>()); }` statements and needs the `sofie` feature `menu`; an entry names a page of its area without parameters.
- An area has no `/` page unless a module routes one; the app answers "Not found." there.
